Atiar Rahman ----- Petitioner
Vs.

full_judgment: 18. In that view of the matter I find that the learned Appellate Judge has fell in serious error in affirming the judgment and decree of dismissal passed by the learned Subordinate Judge dismissing the suit of the plaintiff putting undue and much reliance upon the clause 19 of the said deed of agreement and he arrived at a wrong decision that the "whole contract has become a nullity and on the strength of such invalid contract suit for specific performance of contract is not maintainable". The learned Appellate Judge concurred with this finding of the learned trial Judge which is erroneous view arrived at and taken by both the Courts below. The next points on which the learned Appellate Judge has put his reliance upon and arrived at his finding on the basis of the statement made by defendant No. 4 that is the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna stating that Kaniz Fatema and defendants No. 1 and 2 being Non-Bangladeshi left the country for Pakistan or elsewhere leaving the suit property uncared and the property has been declared as abandoned property and no suit in connection with abandoned property would be proceeded in Civil Court. And the learned Appellate Judge found that "for giving decision in respect of the Abandoned Property special Court i.e. the Settlement Courts have been created and by the Abandoned Property Act the power of Civil Court has been extinguished and ceased to entertain any suit or case. As such this suit is being without jurisdiction of the Civil Court plaintiff would not get any relief as prayed for". After going through the evidence on record I find that the Government defendant No. 4 although claim that the property is an abandoned property but the Government did not produce a single piece of evidence to the effect that the Government at any point of time declared this property as an abandoned property. If it is so, the Government could produced the Gazette notification that has been published by the Government giving full particulars of abandoned property by Bangladesh Gazette notification published in 1985 as well as the final list published in 1986. But nothing of such kind has been produced before the Court nor the defendant No. 4 adduced any witness even to make statement that this property is abandoned property. Moreover, on perusal of the Ext. 1 i.e. bainapatra I find that Kaniz Fatema is the executrix of the bainapatra who is the lessee cum owner of the case property and this bainapatra is a registered instrument which has been registered as per provision of Registration Act being registered deed No. 14857 dated 18-7-1983 wherein her son Atim Ali is an witness, to the execution of the bainapatra as well as he is the identifier of the executrix Kaniz Fatema in the affidavit that has been swear by the executrix with the said deed of agreement before the Sub-Registrar and this Atim Ali identified saying that "দাতা আমার মাতা আমার সামনে সহি করিলেন" So from these two documents and subsequently the Ext. 2 that also having been executed by Kaniz Fatema and both the documents exhibited before the Court being Exts. 1 and 2 clearly shows that the lessee of the said property namely Kaniz Fatema at least she was present in this country till the date of execution and the registration of the said bainapatra dated 18-7-1983 and her son Atim Ali who is now contesting this revisional application as opposite party before this Court is still present in this country. So her property in no way can be declared to be or presumed to be abandoned property while the owner herself was present in this country at least till execution and registration of the said bainapatra and money receipt executed on 25-7-1983 which has been proved by witnesses before the trial Court and the same being exhibited as Exts. No. 1 and 2. In this context I would like to referred to a decision of our Appellate Division being the case of Shishir Kanti Pal vs Nur Muhammad reported in 55 DLR (AD) 39 wherein our lordships of the Appellate Division have found "A registered document carries presumption of correctness of the endorsement made therein-One who disputes this presumption is required to dislodge the correctness of the endorsement."
